domains: Health Informatics & Clinical Decision Support Provenance

entries.citation: Kung HT, Robinson JT. On Optimistic Methods for Concurrency Control. ACM Transactions on Database Systems (TODS). 1981;6(2):213-226. DOI: 10.1145/319566.319567
entries.read_state_semantics: Transactions read freely from the database without acquiring shared read locks; read sets are tracked in memory.
entries.write_semantics: Writes are staged locally in a private write buffer and applied to the shared store only during the write phase after successful validation.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: None. Pure database storage concurrency without authorization or privacy semantics.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Read set (RS) and write set (WS) intersection validation against concurrently committed transactions.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) with backward/forward validation phases.
entries.what_it_establishes: Establishes validation-at-commit: transactions execute optimistically and validate that read dependencies have not been invalidated by concurrent writes prior to durable persistence.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes any claim that commit-time conflict detection, staging updates in private buffers, or validating read sets before write commits is novel. OCC has been foundational systems art for over 45 years.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: OCC only checks whether raw database tuples have changed. GRWC addresses a decoupled, non-deterministic inference step: verifying that the persistent mutation proposal was produced by an inference lineage that actually consumed the exact model-visible governed disclosure projection, while database state and governance are independently revalidated.

entries.citation: Cahill MJ, Röhm U, Fekete AD. Serializable Snapshot Isolation in PostgreSQL. In: Proceedings of the 2008 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data (SIGMOD '08). 2008:729-738. DOI: 10.1145/1376616.1376690
entries.read_state_semantics: Transactions read from a consistent multiversion snapshot established at transaction start.
entries.write_semantics: Writes create new versions; dangerous structures (consecutive rw-antidependency edges in the serialization graph) trigger aborts.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: None. Relational isolation guarantees only.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: SIREAD lock tracking detects write-skew and anti-dependencies between read snapshots and concurrent commits.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI).
entries.what_it_establishes: Proves that snapshot isolation can be extended to guarantee true serializability without blocking reads, by tracking dependency cycles dynamically at commit.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that snapshot-based reads combined with commit-time anti-dependency checks or detecting write skew are novel contributions.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: SSI detects database-level rw-cycles across active DB transactions. It cannot reason about external LLM inference epochs, prompt disclosure projections, or whether an out-of-band AI reasoning agent consumed superseded patient clinical history.

entries.citation: Ports DRK, Grittner K. Serializable Snapshot Isolation in PostgreSQL. Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment (PVLDB). 2012;5(12):1850-1861. DOI: 10.14778/2367502.2367527
entries.read_state_semantics: Predicate locks and tuple-level lock flags in shared memory tracking PostgreSQL snapshot reads.
entries.write_semantics: Engine-level commit aborts on detected cycle; tuple versioning with heap visibility rules.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: None.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Lock-free conflict flags and summary locks tracking rw-antidependencies in PostgreSQL engine.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Production-grade relational SSI inside PostgreSQL.
entries.what_it_establishes: Demonstrates practical production-scale serializable snapshot isolation in PostgreSQL with minimal overhead.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that PostgreSQL-backed serializability, row locking, or avoiding TOCTOU in relational storage is a novel research contribution.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: PostgreSQL SSI ensures ACID consistency for internal SQL statements. GLHS addresses the cross-layer boundary where an external AI worker generates medical mutations over minutes; GLHS uses PostgreSQL's transactional primitives as an execution substrate, not a novel database engine contribution.

entries.citation: Yu X, Pavlo A, Sanchez D, Devadas S. TicToc: Time-Traveling Optimistic Concurrency Control. In: Proceedings of the 2016 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data (SIGMOD '16). 2016:1629-1642. DOI: 10.1145/2882903.2915243
entries.read_state_semantics: Data items carry read and write timestamps; reads track logical valid intervals dynamically.
entries.write_semantics: Writes update valid intervals, computing valid commit timestamps without a centralized timestamp allocation.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: None.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Dynamic timestamp intervals compute valid commit timestamps covering all read/write sets.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Data-driven timestamp-based OCC.
entries.what_it_establishes: Shows that timestamp-based OCC can avoid aborts by lazily discovering whether a read snapshot was logically consistent without central bottlenecks.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that version timestamp intervals, dynamic validation of read validity, or timestamp-based commit gating is novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: TicToc computes logical database timestamps for internal memory tuples. GRWC validates whether an AI proposal's lineage is rooted in an exact, signed disclosure projection supplied to an LLM provider and revalidates dynamic governance.

entries.citation: Agrawal R, Kiernan J, Srikant R, Xu Y. Hippocratic Databases. In: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Very Large Data Bases (VLDB '02). 2002:143-154. DOI: 10.1016/B978-155860869-6/50021-3
entries.read_state_semantics: Queries must declare purpose, recipient, and access credentials; data tables specify purpose specifications and retention policies.
entries.write_semantics: Updates must comply with privacy metadata; deletion triggered by retention expiration.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: First-class database privacy policies, purpose-specification tables, and patient consent directives.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Purpose matching: data read for Purpose P cannot be processed or re-stored for Purpose Q without fresh authorization.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Standard RDBMS concurrency underneath policy filters.
entries.what_it_establishes: Pioneered Hippocratic Databases where purpose-specification, patient consent, limited disclosure, and auditability are embedded directly in the data management system.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming novelty for purpose-restricted health data access, consent-gated tables, or privacy policies inside clinical database systems.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: Hippocratic Databases enforce purpose boundaries on query disclosure. GRWC enforces that when an AI system synthesizes new persistent records based on disclosed data, the resulting write is admitted only if the inference lineage verifiably received that exact disclosure and current governance/state remains unviolated at commit.

entries.citation: Byun JW, Li N. Purpose based access control for privacy protection in relational database systems. The VLDB Journal. 2008;17(4):603-619. DOI: 10.1007/s00778-006-0023-0
entries.read_state_semantics: Data elements associated with intended purpose hierarchies; query evaluation enforces intended purpose subsumes access purpose.
entries.write_semantics: Data insertions associate intended purpose attributes with attribute values.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Hierarchical purpose trees and conditional purpose access control (PBAC) policies.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Access purpose validated against stored intended purpose; policy ensures legitimate usage across tasks.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Standard relational transaction processing.
entries.what_it_establishes: Formalized Purpose-Based Access Control (PBAC) for relational databases, defining exact semantics for purpose hierarchies and role-purpose bindings.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that purpose-based access control, task/purpose attributes on queries, or hierarchical purpose gating is a novel invention of GLHS.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: PBAC gates data queries based on declared purpose. GRWC binds the inference-time purpose/task to the proposal's cryptographic lineage and verifies at write-admission time that the actor, role, purpose, and task remain valid under the current policy state.

entries.citation: Park J, Sandhu R. The UCON_ABC usage control model. ACM Transactions on Information and System Security (TISSEC). 2004;7(1):128-174. DOI: 10.1145/984334.984339
entries.read_state_semantics: Continuous authorization evaluating Subject Attributes, Object Attributes, and System Rights.
entries.write_semantics: State changes update mutable attributes; violations revoke ongoing usage.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: UCON encompasses authorizations (A), obligations (B), and conditions (C), with pre-evaluations and ongoing evaluations.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Continuous monitoring connects initial access permissions to subsequent operations.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Attribute state updates and event-driven policy enforcement.
entries.what_it_establishes: Unified model of usage control defining pre-decision, ongoing-decision, and attribute-mutation invariants across system lifecycles.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that continuous revalidation, condition monitoring, or combining pre-access checks with post-action checks is conceptually novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: UCON focuses on continuous consumption/rendering of digital objects (e.g., streaming DRM, active sessions). GRWC bridges the semantic gap between an unmonitored external LLM inference step and an atomic database commit of AI-generated clinical mutations.

entries.citation: Garg D, Jia L, Datta A. A Proof-Carrying File System. In: 2010 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP). 2010:549-564. DOI: 10.1109/SP.2010.28
entries.read_state_semantics: File read requests require machine-checkable constructive proofs of authorization derived from authorization logic.
entries.write_semantics: Write requests accompany formal proofs that the writer possesses authorized write permissions at the target inode.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Decentralized logic-based authorization policies (BL logic) proving access conformance.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Proofs attest to valid capabilities, delegations, and access rights across distributed file operations.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Proof validation integrated into the file system VFS/kernel layer before disk execution.
entries.what_it_establishes: Demonstrates proof-carrying authorization in systems: access requests supply machine-verifiable cryptographic/logical proofs that are self-contained and independently checked at admission.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that bundling machine-verifiable proofs or authorization tokens with write requests is novel. Proof-carrying authorization is established prior art.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: PCFS proves authorization of the actor to write. GRWC carries a consumption proof that the write proposal was derived from a specific, attested governed disclosure projection, combined with dynamic re-evaluation of medical consent and dependency freshness.

entries.citation: Birgisson A, Politz JG, Erlingsson Ú, Taly A, Vrable M, Lentczner M. Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud. In: 21st Annual Network and Distributed System Security Symposium (NDSS '14). 2014. DOI: 10.14722/ndss.2014.23212
entries.read_state_semantics: Bearer presents token with attenuated first-party and third-party caveats.
entries.write_semantics: Target verifies HMAC chain of caveats; request admitted only if all context caveats hold.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Decentralized caveat attenuation: time limits, IP restrictions, purpose caveats, third-party discharge tokens.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Cryptographic HMAC chaining binds initial capability to attenuated contextual caveats.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Target-side stateless verification at request receipt.
entries.what_it_establishes: Establishes contextual capability tokens: flexible, attenuatable, cryptographically chained bearer tokens that enforce dynamic context caveats at request verification.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that cryptographic capability tokens, caveat chaining, or context-bound request authorization is novel. It also mandates that GLHS cannot claim THSS is uniquely necessary, requiring a minimal token comparator.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: Macaroons verify that a caller holds an attenuated capability. GLHS solves the complementary problem of verifying that a proposed clinical state transition was generated from an exact, bounded disclosure supplied to an external model inference, and that the clinical underlying state has not drifted.

entries.citation: Green TJ, Karvounarakis G, Tannen V. Provenance Semirings. In: Proceedings of the Twenty-Sixth ACM SIGMOD-SIGACT-SIGART Symposium on Principles of Database Systems (PODS '07). 2007:31-40. DOI: 10.1145/1265530.1265535
entries.read_state_semantics: Source relations annotated with commutative semiring polynomials representing lineage.
entries.write_semantics: Relational algebra operations propagate polynomials, yielding algebraic derivation provenance for output views.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Can model trust, security levels, and probabilistic lineage via semiring valuations.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Algebraic semiring expressions form exact mathematical derivations linking input tuples to output tuples.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Static relational algebra evaluation.
entries.what_it_establishes: Foundational formal framework for data provenance: provides mathematical semantics for how input annotations propagate through relational transformations into output derivations.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming novelty for provenance representation, derivation tracking, or algebraic lineage linking inputs to outputs.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: Semirings track deterministic algebraic operators (selection, join, projection). GRWC handles non-deterministic neural LLM inference where the transformation cannot be expressed as an algebraic formula, but where the exact input disclosure coordinate must be verified during transaction admission.

entries.citation: Bates A, Tian DJ, Butler KRB, Moyer T. Trustworthy Whole-System Provenance for the Linux Kernel. In: 24th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 15). 2015:319-334.
entries.read_state_semantics: LSM hooks capture OS-level read, memory-map, and IPC events as provenance graph nodes.
entries.write_semantics: LSM hooks intercept write and network operations, verifying that whole-system provenance invariants are maintained.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Reference monitor enforcement of system security policies based on live kernel provenance.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Kernel IPC/file causality graph binds process inputs to process outputs.
entries.concurrency_semantics: OS kernel reference monitor synchronized with kernel lock structures.
entries.what_it_establishes: Proves that provenance is not merely an offline post-hoc audit log, but can be enforced actively by an in-kernel reference monitor to gate system transitions.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that 'using provenance as an active enforcement mechanism rather than an audit log' is an original discovery of GLHS. Active provenance enforcement is established systems art.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: LPM enforces OS information-flow control across processes. GRWC operates at the semantic application/EHR boundary, enforcing that AI health mutations preserve read-to-write continuity across non-deterministic LLM calls while revalidating clinical consent and bitemporal state.

entries.citation: Moreau L, Missier P, et al. PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model. W3C Recommendation. World Wide Web Consortium. 2013. https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/
entries.read_state_semantics: Entities represent physical, digital, or conceptual states.
entries.write_semantics: Activities generate entities and are associated with agents through formal provenance relations (wasDerivedFrom, wasGeneratedBy, used, wasAssociatedWith).
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Can be augmented with provenance access policies and attribution metadata.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Relations `used(activity, entity)` and `wasGeneratedBy(entity, activity)` establish explicit input-output binding.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Graph representation standard.
entries.what_it_establishes: Global standard for interoperable provenance interchange, modeling entities, activities, agents, and their derivation relations.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that modeling AI outputs as derived from inputs, activities, and agent prompts is a novel contribution.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: W3C PROV is a descriptive data model. GLHS specifies an operational commit-admission invariant that gates database transactions on exact disclosure bindings and revalidates dynamic governance.

entries.citation: Curcin V, Fairweather E, Danger R, Corrigan D. Templates as a method for implementing data provenance in decision support systems. Journal of Biomedical Informatics (JBI). 2017;65:1-21. DOI: 10.1016/j.jbi.2016.10.022
entries.area: Health Informatics & Clinical Decision Support Provenance
entries.read_state_semantics: Clinical decision support systems ingest EHR observations matching predefined clinical guideline templates.
entries.write_semantics: Generated recommendations capture execution traces and link back to instantiated guideline templates.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Audit trails for clinical compliance and guideline attribution.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Template-based provenance graphs explicitly link clinical inputs to DSS recommendations.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Execution tracing within clinical workflow engines.
entries.what_it_establishes: Establishes structured clinical decision support provenance: demonstrates how clinical guidelines and input observations must be captured as provenance templates for clinical safety and auditability.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that capturing clinical evidence, DSS input provenance, or decision traces in health informatics is a novel concept.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: Curcin et al. construct provenance traces for deterministic rule-based CDSS for post-hoc audit. GRWC evaluates whether persistent mutations proposed by probabilistic LLM agents are atomically admissible at commit time based on exact disclosure and concurrent state drift.

entries.citation: Margheri A, Masi M, Milani F, Sassone V. Decentralised provenance for healthcare data. International Journal of Medical Informatics (IJMI). 2020;141:104197. DOI: 10.1016/j.ijmedinf.2020.104197
entries.area: Health Informatics & Clinical Decision Support Provenance
entries.read_state_semantics: Distributed healthcare records read across decentralized entities under consent contracts.
entries.write_semantics: Healthcare events recorded in tamper-evident distributed logs with cryptographic commitments.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Patient consent smart contracts govern data sharing and access permissions.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Cryptographic transaction hashes bind healthcare data access events to subsequent records.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Distributed ledger consensus.
entries.what_it_establishes: Demonstrates the combination of cryptographic tamper-evident logging, healthcare provenance, and dynamic patient consent in clinical data sharing.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that combining patient consent, cryptographic hashing, and provenance in healthcare is novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: Margheri et al. use blockchain logs for cross-organizational audit of human-initiated data exchanges. GLHS solves local application-server-to-database TOCTOU and exact-disclosure admission for autonomous AI agent persistent state writes.

entries.citation: HL7 International. FHIR Release 5: Provenance and AuditEvent Resources. Health Level Seven International; 2024. Available from: http://hl7.org/fhir/R5/provenance.html
entries.area: Health Informatics & Clinical Decision Support Provenance
entries.read_state_semantics: EHR resources referenced by canonical URI and versionId (`Observation/123/_history/1`).
entries.write_semantics: RESTful resource commits record target, agent, entity, and signature elements in `Provenance` resources.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Security labels and FHIR `Consent` resource references.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: `Provenance.entity` role codes (`derivation`, `revision`, `quotation`, `source`) bind target resources to source resources.
entries.concurrency_semantics: HTTP ETag headers (`If-Match: W/"version"`) provide basic OCC.
entries.what_it_establishes: Standardizes health data versioning, ETag-based optimistic locking, and provenance recording in clinical healthcare standards.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that linking clinical records to versioned source entities or using ETag OCC in health systems is a new contribution.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: FHIR ETags only check whether the target resource was modified. They cannot verify whether the exact subset of clinical attributes exposed in an AI prompt envelope remains valid when an LLM proposal arrives 30 seconds later.

entries.citation: Kaye J, Whitley EA, Lund D, Morrison M, Teare H, Melham K. Dynamic consent: a patient interface for twenty-first century research networks. European Journal of Human Genetics (EJHG). 2015;23(2):141-146. DOI: 10.1038/ejhg.2014.71
entries.read_state_semantics: Patient longitudinal biobank records accessed under dynamic, fine-grained consent preferences.
entries.write_semantics: Patient updates consent preferences in real-time through an interactive digital interface.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Continuous, granular, revocable consent directives replacing static broad consent.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Consent status dynamically checked prior to biobank and research data inclusion.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Web portal state updates.
entries.what_it_establishes: Foundational concept of Dynamic Consent in healthcare: patient consent is mutable, granular, and must be continuously respected as preferences change over time.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that dynamic, versioned, or revocable patient consent is a novel invention of GLHS.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: Kaye et al. define the patient-facing governance paradigm. GLHS operationalizes this paradigm into a transactional systems invariant (GRWC), guaranteeing that if a patient revokes consent while an AI model is reasoning, the resulting proposal is atomically rejected at commit.

entries.citation: Lekadir K, Osuala R, Gallin C, et al. FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare. BMJ. 2025;388:e081554. DOI: 10.1136/bmj-2024-081554
entries.read_state_semantics: Clinical AI lifecycle data ingestion requiring Fairness, Universality, Traceability, Usability, Robustness, and Explainability.
entries.write_semantics: Clinical deployments must maintain audited logs of model versions, operational contexts, and safety guardrails.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Comprehensive regulatory and ethical AI governance guidelines.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Traceability principles mandate linking clinical recommendations to inputs and model versions.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Organizational governance protocols.
entries.what_it_establishes: Premier consensus guideline establishing six core principles (FUTURE-AI) for healthcare AI deployment, demanding rigorous end-to-end traceability and governance.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that advocating for healthcare AI traceability, auditability, or governance is a novel research finding.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: FUTURE-AI provides high-level ethical and deployment requirements. GLHS provides a concrete, machine-enforced transactional commit kernel that enforces the Traceability and Robustness requirements at the systems database layer.

entries.citation: Sendak M, Gao M, et al. SMART: structured, meaningful, auditable, responsible, and transparent documentation for clinical AI. Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association (JAMIA). 2026;33(2):ocag117. DOI: 10.1093/jamia/ocag117
entries.read_state_semantics: Documentation captures training datasets, model versions, intended clinical use, and performance metrics.
entries.write_semantics: Auditable model cards and runtime monitoring records archived for clinical governance.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Structured accountability frameworks for clinical decision algorithms.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Clinical AI documentation binds model capabilities and limitations to specific clinical contexts.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Governance documentation lifecycle.
entries.what_it_establishes: Defines the clinical standard for auditable, responsible, and transparent clinical AI documentation throughout its operational lifecycle.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that clinical AI documentation, model metadata recording, or audit trails are novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: SMART operates at the documentation and organizational level. GLHS is a runtime execution and commit mechanism that embeds model metadata into an immutable cryptographic inference binding enforced during persistent state mutations.

entries.citation: Wu J, et al. LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory. In: The Thirteenth International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2025). 2025.
entries.tier: CORE A* / Top Machine Learning Venue
entries.read_state_semantics: Agents retrieve longitudinal multi-session chat histories across temporal horizons.
entries.write_semantics: Memory updates insert, modify, or supersede previous conversational facts.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Evaluates accuracy of memory update and temporal consistency; no clinical consent model.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Evaluates factual continuity across multi-turn interactions.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Single-agent sequential benchmark.
entries.what_it_establishes: Standardizes benchmark evaluation for long-term interactive memory in LLM assistants, demonstrating significant failure rates in fact updates, temporal reasoning, and contradiction handling.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that long-term agent memory or tracking temporal state updates in LLM conversations is novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: LongMemEval evaluates whether LLMs accurately retrieve updated facts in conversational context. GLHS provides the database and systems commit protocol ensuring that mutations generated by memory agents cannot violate concurrency, consent, or disclosure bounds.

entries.citation: Wang B, et al. Unveiling Privacy Risks in LLM Agent Memory. In: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2025). 2025.
entries.read_state_semantics: Memory store stores persistent user secrets and preferences across conversations.
entries.write_semantics: Adversarial prompts trigger leakage or unauthorized extraction of persistent memory records.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Identifies severe privacy leakage when agent memory lacks isolation and access controls.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Prompt injection bridges user input to persistent memory retrieval and extraction.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Multi-turn agent execution.
entries.what_it_establishes: Demonstrates that persistent agent memory is an acute privacy attack vector: without strict disclosure control and isolation, agents inadvertently leak stored user secrets across interactions.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Motivates the critical need for memory access governance, but proves that memory privacy risks are recognized prior art.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: Wang et al. uncover memory extraction vulnerabilities. GLHS directly addresses this threat by bounding model-visible memory to exact, signed projections and enforcing strict purpose/task access control on both reads and persistent writes.

entries.citation: Li X, et al. MemTX: Transactional Belief Commit for Stateful Agent Memory. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.23929. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Belief records carry evidence, permissions, provenance, and validity metadata under snapshot-isolated reads.
entries.write_semantics: Validate-and-commit pipeline stages belief records in private workspaces and gates irreversible tool calls; retraction triggers cascading repair.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Permissions and validity metadata stored as record attributes; no healthcare consent or dynamic patient revocation model.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Belief lifecycle states (staged, committed, retracted) bind belief updates to irreversible action gating.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Snapshot-isolated transactions with machine-checked state-machine properties and bounded model checking.
entries.what_it_establishes: Introduces transactional belief commit for stateful agent memory, staging updates in private workspaces and validating dependencies before committing durable changes or tool calls.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes GLHS from claiming novelty for transactional commit pipelines for agent memory, staging updates, stale-write prevention, belief retraction, or bounded formal checking of agent commit states.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: MemTX focuses on generic belief consistency and tool gating. GLHS addresses the health-specific invariant GRWC: binding persistent mutations to the exact model-visible governed disclosure projection supplied to inference, and revalidating dynamic clinical consent and bitemporal state against concurrent clinical writers in PostgreSQL.

entries.citation: Cui Y, et al. MemTxn: A Transaction Boundary for Source-Supported Updates and Complete-State Recovery in Agent Memory. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.27834. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Temporal Resolver selects visible memory versions under a declared chronology contract.
entries.write_semantics: Ordered PatchTest admits source-supported updates; durable snapshot journal recovers active state upon failure.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Evidence support and source provenance are required inputs for patch admission; no health consent lifecycle.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Source citation supports the proposed update; checks whether proposed facts have supporting citations in the underlying knowledge source.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Conflict detection, version resolution, and state recovery journal.
entries.what_it_establishes: Defines a transaction boundary for source-supported memory updates, requiring proposed facts to cite supporting sources and maintaining recovery journals.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes GLHS from claiming novelty for source-supported updates, citation checking, temporal version selection, or snapshot recovery journals.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: MemTxn checks whether a fact is supported by *some* source in the knowledge base (global source support). GLHS enforces *exact consumed disclosure*: it is not enough that an evidence item exists in the patient chart; the proposal is rejected if that evidence was not part of the exact governed disclosure projection supplied to that specific inference lineage.

entries.citation: Ren H, et al. GateMem: Benchmarking Memory Governance in Multi-Principal Shared-Memory Agents. arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.18829. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Multi-principal episodic memory queried under roles, scopes, and relationships at hidden checkpoints.
entries.write_semantics: Evaluates memory updates and active forgetting at the agent interface under adversarial privacy prompts.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Contextual access-control boundaries and deletion requests evaluated across principals.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Evaluates disclosure governance and updates, but does not provide an atomic systems transaction boundary.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Incremental memory injection and checkpoint evaluation.
entries.what_it_establishes: Establishes a benchmark for memory governance in multi-principal agent environments, evaluating scope leakage and forgetting compliance.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that evaluating multi-principal memory access, role boundaries, or memory forgetting in agent systems is novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: GateMem is an empirical benchmark evaluating prompt-level leakage. GLHS is an operational systems commit kernel enforcing cryptographic read-to-write continuity and database atomicity.

entries.citation: Anon. Cordon: Semantic Transactions for Tool-Using LLM Agents. arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.17573. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Task-scoped semantic transaction tracks tool intents, result lineage, and shadow state.
entries.write_semantics: Stages external effects in an outbox and validates composed execution before commit or release.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Delegated authority stored as transaction metadata; no health consent or patient revocation semantics.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Task transaction binds tool lineage, authority, staged state, and external effects.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Commit/recovery semantics and containment invariants across multi-step agent workflows.
entries.what_it_establishes: Establishes task-scoped semantic transactions for agent tool calls, staging side effects in an outbox and validating composed execution before release.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming novelty for task-scoped semantic transactions, staging tool effects, rollback/recovery, or lineage-aware outbox commitments.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: Cordon manages multi-step tool call staging. GLHS manages longitudinal patient health state mutations, ensuring that the model's clinical proposals are admitted only when continuous with the exact governed clinical disclosure projection.

entries.citation: Anon. TOKI: A Bitemporal Operator Algebra for Contradiction Resolution in LLM-Agent Persistent Memory. arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.06240. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Versioned facts carry valid time, system time, provenance, and isolation preconditions.
entries.write_semantics: Typed contradiction-resolution operators write dual rows (valid and system time) and preserve losing facts in audit rows.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Per-rule policy is an operator parameter; no healthcare consent lifecycle.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Operator contracts bind write-time isolation and provenance to temporal fact supersession.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Soundness across bitemporal schema, multi-writer contention, and write-time anomaly analysis.
entries.what_it_establishes: Formulates a bitemporal operator algebra for resolving contradictions in persistent agent memory while preserving losing facts in audit trails.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that bitemporal state (valid time vs system time), preserving historical fact versions, or typed contradiction resolution in agent memory is novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: TOKI resolves internal memory fact contradictions using bitemporal algebra. GLHS resolves the authority and freshness of clinical proposals against external concurrent EHR writers and dynamic consent changes.

entries.citation: Anon. Temporary Authority, Permanent Effects: Commit-Time Authorization for LLM Agents. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.10487. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Authority witnesses (DOM snapshots, approval epochs, version tokens) captured during execution.
entries.write_semantics: Fail-closed commit-boundary monitor refreshes, rebinds, replans, or refuses actions before durable effect.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Authority freshness, causal priority binding, and eligibility checked at commit.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Explicit witness-to-effect binding validates authority freshness before applying side effects.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Fail-closed commit-boundary monitoring.
entries.what_it_establishes: Demonstrates commit-time authorization for LLM agents, revalidating authority witnesses before executing durable actions to prevent stale authorization.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that commit-time authorization, revalidating stale authority before write, or fail-closed commit monitors are novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: CommitGuard monitors user approval tokens for tool execution. GLHS binds the exact data disclosure projection provided to model inference, enforcing dependency completeness and revalidating clinical consent in a production database transaction.

entries.citation: Peng J, Wu L. Stateful Governance for Concurrent Agentic Systems. arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.02764. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Policy programs evaluate operations against mutable policy state.
entries.write_semantics: Provider contracts coordinate policy state and effects so committed effects remain authorized at commit time.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Stateful policy programs with dynamic transitions.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Policy-state serializability ensures operations are authorized under the policy state active at commit.
entries.concurrency_semantics: PostgreSQL-backed prototype coordinating policy state and effect execution.
entries.what_it_establishes: Introduces stateful governance and policy-state serializability, ensuring agent effects remain authorized against evolving policy state in PostgreSQL.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that coordinating policy state and effects in PostgreSQL or preventing stale policy authorization is novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: MasuGate validates that an effect conforms to the current policy program. GLHS enforces that the persistent health mutation proposal is rooted in the specific governed disclosure consumed by inference, preventing undisclosed evidence poisoning and route downgrade.

entries.citation: Margalit O, et al. Governed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent LLM Systems. arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.24535. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Scoped retrieval over multi-tenant fleet memory under dynamic sharing policies.
entries.write_semantics: Policy-governed propagation with provenance tracking and derivation chain audit.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Role and tenant-scoped retrieval policies.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Derivation chains track how retrieved memories propagate across agent collaboration sessions.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Distributed REST evaluation of memory propagation.
entries.what_it_establishes: Demonstrates governed shared memory for multi-agent systems, enforcing retrieval scoping and tracking propagation provenance across agents.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming novelty for scoped agent memory retrieval, provenance-tracked memory propagation, or multi-agent memory governance.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: MemClaw governs memory sharing across agent fleets. GLHS enforces an atomic admission invariant on persistent clinical state mutations within a clinical EHR ecosystem.

entries.citation: Li Z, et al. A Self-Evolving Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.13940. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Private longitudinal memory stores profile facts, reusable procedures, and episodic health traces.
entries.write_semantics: Self-evolving updates mutate profile/procedure/episodic memories after health consultation episodes.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: Separation of private health context and safety guidelines; prompt-level guardrails.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Selective persistence based on post-episode induction heuristics.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Single-user sequential longitudinal consultation episodes.
entries.what_it_establishes: Demonstrates a self-evolving longitudinal personal health agent that updates long-term health memories across consultations.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that longitudinal personal health memory, episodic health tracking, or updating patient health profiles via LLMs is novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: HealthClaw relies on unverified prompt heuristics and single-user storage. GLHS provides rigorous database-level concurrency control, exact-disclosure binding, dependency derivation, and dynamic consent revalidation under multi-writer clinical contention.

entries.citation: Anon. Verified Detection and Prevention of Concurrency Anomalies in Multi-Agent Large Language Model Systems. arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.17182. 2026.
entries.read_state_semantics: Long-running read-generate-write operations over shared memory, vector indices, and tool registries.
entries.write_semantics: Verified runtimes detect/prevent stale generation, phantom tools, and causal cascade anomalies.
entries.policy_or_consent_semantics: None; focused on execution concurrency anomalies.
entries.binding_between_read_and_write: Read-generate-write lineage is central to anomaly definitions and lock-based execution levels.
entries.concurrency_semantics: Formal TLA+ anomaly catalog, Verus proofs, snapshot isolation, and multi-version locking.
entries.what_it_establishes: Formalizes concurrency anomalies in multi-agent LLM systems and proves safety properties of multi-level concurrency control runtimes using TLA+ and Verus.
entries.why_it_precludes_false_novelty_claim: Precludes claiming that identifying read-generate-write race conditions, formalizing agent concurrency anomalies in TLA+, or snapshot isolation for agents is novel.
entries.glhs_novelty_boundary_differentiation: Verified Concurrency Runtimes catalog generic agent memory execution anomalies. GLHS solves the medical informatics governance problem: establishing that AI-generated clinical records must satisfy Governed Read-to-Write Continuity (GRWC) over dynamic clinical consent, bitemporal EHR states, and exact model-visible disclosures.
